ledger.note: 11 August 1786: Penang becomes British. 'Light was ordered to acquire Penang Island from Kedah'; Light's party 'arrived on 17 July 1786'; 'a ceremony was held on 11 August, during which the Union Jack was raised for the first time'; the Sultan agreed 'in return for British military assistance and a lease payment' of 6,000 Spanish dollars; the island was renamed Prince of Wales Island and the settlement George Town (the page gives the renaming without a date).

region.text: Seberang Perai (Province Wellesley), the mainland strip opposite Penang

ledger.note: 1800: Province Wellesley. 'In 1800, the first Lieutenant-Governor of Prince of Wales Island, Sir George Leith, gained a 189.3 km2 (73.1 sq mi) strip' of Seberang Perai from the Sultan of Kedah, with permanent British sovereignty over the island and the strip and the annual payment raised to 10,000 Spanish dollars; the Seberang Perai page: 'the territory ... was ceded to the British East India Company in 1800'. The Kedah dossier gives 7 July 1800 from the Kedah page; this page has only the year.
1805: Penang is made a separate Presidency. 'Penang was administered under the Bengal Presidency until 1805, when Penang was made a separate Presidency on par with Madras, Bombay and Bengal.'

ledger.note: 1826: Penang is amalgamated into the Straits Settlements. 'In 1826, the British East India Company amalgamated the territories of Penang, Singapore (acquired from Johor in 1819) and Malacca (acquired from the Netherlands in 1824)'; George Town became the administrative and judicial capital of the new entity (capital until 1832).

certainty.note: An island and a mainland strip fixed by treaty (the Perai river as the border, per the Kedah dossier's reading of the Penang page).

sources.title: History of Penang
sources.note: Light's acquisition in 1786 (arrival 17 July, ceremony 11 August), the renaming as Prince of Wales Island, Province Wellesley of 189.3 km2 in 1800, separate Presidency in 1805, amalgamation into the Straits Settlements in 1826 with George Town as capital.

sources.title: Seberang Perai
sources.note: The mainland strip ceded to the East India Company in 1800 for 4,000 Spanish dollars (page text), later extended in 1831 and 1868; total land mass 747.8 km2.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch: the straits-settlements dossier starts in 1826 and the sultanate-of-kedah dossier records the 1786 and 1800 losses to british-colonial-empire; this dossier gives the Presidency its own life. Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the 1786 date: the page has arrival on 17 July and a ceremony on 11 August; the dossier starts in August, as the Kedah dossier does; (2) the 1800 cession: the page gives the year only (the Kedah dossier has 7 July 1800 from another page), and the payment 4,000 Spanish dollars (Seberang Perai page) against 10,000 per annum (History of Penang) are two different sums; (3) the renaming as Prince of Wales Island is undated on the page and not made an event; (4) the Siamese invasion of Kedah in 1821 is mentioned without a date and is not recorded; (5) the island's area is not on the pages; the shape is a 14 km disc, as in the Kedah dossier; (6) the later extensions of Province Wellesley (1831, 1868, 1874 Dindings) fall after 1826, in the straits-settlements dossier; (7) the counterpart for Kedah's two losses reads british-colonial-empire and should read this slug; (8) British Singapore (1819-1826, 'acquired from Johor in 1819' on the page) have no dossier of their own before 1826; Malacca under British occupation from 1795 is carried as an occupation event in the dutch-malacca dossier, and the page dates its acquisition from the Netherlands to 1824. Gazetteer: Pulau Pinang (admin1, Malaysia) and George Town (place) resolve already.
